title: Barnet's band: Ellington arrangements and records
summary: After the Barnet library burned, Ellington sent arrangements; Leeman played as if he had always known the book and they cut 'Blue Juice' and 'Charleston Alley'.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: But when I sat in Barnet's band, they got burned out in California, Duke was sending them arrangements because he loved Charlie so much, and I sat in the band as if I had played in it all my life, because I knew whatever they were going to play -- I'd know it, and so Charlie never said a word to me except 'play.'

And then I had my freedom musically, and I was with him almost two years before I went with -- we will get into that little by little, but he made some tremendous things with several Barnet bands, record dates I'm talking about like 'Blue Juice' and 'Charleston Alley' and 'Little Smack' was writing for us then, Horace Henderson was giving us arrangements for Charlie Barnett.

Let's just digress for a minute, because this has been beautiful, and I'm so happy that you enlightened us, and so many people have profited by this because the fact that you showed how you developed into
The band's library was destroyed in a fire.

such a great musician and this is why you are equally great, and as great as all of the musicians you've copied from -- well, not really copied, but listened to, and learned from. And you've turned out to be a fine musician.
Well, I was fortunate enough to be with these people, too.

And this is what all of learning is about. Now we are supposed to be better than the people we learn from because we have a better opportunity to express ourselves, and as you said, that you had a chance with Charlie Barnet after hearing all these people, you had a chance to exercise -- Charlie was gracious enough to give you the chance to exercise, to do the things that you wanted to do.
And this was where you began to develop ...
